relevance_note: The paper reports two brothers with succinic semialdehyde dehydrogenase (SSADH) deficiency, one with an ALDH5A1 genotype, stating "We report the occurrence of an unusual paroxysmal movement disorder in two affected siblings born of healthy nonconsanguineous Italian parents."
method_note: Hand transcription (no script used); every span was copied from the Markdown file and re-checked. Two in-scope people: the paper's own labels "Case 1" and "Case 2" (used as individual_label_in_paper). The parents are only described as "healthy nonconsanguineous Italian parents"; they are not stated to be tested and are not described as affected, so under Scope they get no rows. The table "Table Metabolic and molecular alterations" has patients as rows in a "Patients" column labelled 1 and 2; I take table patient 1 = Case 1 and table patient 2 = Case 2 because the table is introduced for the two reported cases, but the paper never states this mapping. In that table the ALDH5A1 genotype cell holds two variants stacked in one cell ("c.278G>T (p.C93F) c.526G>A (p.G176R)") on the row of patient 1, while the corresponding cell on the row of patient 2 is empty; I did not distribute the two variants by position, so both variant rows are attached to the patient row that prints them and Case 2 keeps a variant row with variant_original_string = not reported (the paper ties an ALDH5A1 genotype to Case 2 only through the empty table cell and the plural statements "The missense alterations on the ALDH5A1 gene cause a markedly reduced enzyme activity in our cases" and "patients homozygous for the two mutations were severely affected"). The paper never states zygosity, parental testing or inheritance, and it gives no formal classification word (pathogenic/VUS) for the variants; "missense alterations" is the authors' own description and "cause a markedly reduced enzyme activity in our cases" is the closest functional statement, both quoted with the sentence in which they appear. No phenotypic_features rows were emitted for the quantitative laboratory values in the table (urine/plasma/CSF GHB, free CSF GABA, enzyme activity), because these are not clinical features and their support sits in a table row whose cells belong to the patient printed on that row. The brain-MRS sentence ("N-Acetylaspartate, choline, creatine/phosphocreatine, and myo-inositol were all normal") and the karyotype sentence ("Cytogenetic analysis disclosed a normal 46 XY karyotype") name no person and no explicit group, so they were not turned into excluded rows. Both paragraphs of this article file contain ">" character entities; spans that include them are copied exactly as they appear in the file. Not found anywhere in the file: "PED" and "generalized seizure". Sections of this article file that belong to other, unrelated articles (palinacousis, Alexander disease) were ignored.
